intent: I bought my camera with the basic kit lens a year ago and now everyone tells me the lens matters more than the body. But the lenses they recommend cost two or three times what my whole camera did. Is expensive glass genuinely sharper in a way I'd see in normal prints and web posts, or is there a middle tier where the improvement mostly stops? I'd love to understand what physically makes one lens better than another, because right now aperture numbers and coating buzzwords mean nothing to me. People who upgraded and regretted it, or didn't, must exist. End with the one lens purchase you'd actually make in my shoes.

intent_v1_legacy: I keep repeating things about recycling that I've just accepted without ever questioning, and lately I'm not sure any of them are actually true. Like, is every type of plastic really recyclable if I toss it in the bin? Can composting genuinely handle all my food waste? Is paper always fine? Does recycling even save more energy than it uses up, and is old electronic junk really recyclable and non-toxic? Can you actually check these one by one and tell me which hold up and which are basically wishful thinking?
